labels.label: theo:backward_policy
labels.notes: No ** mark here, which is correct: the label stays marked once, in EGF/BackwardPolicy.lean (EGF.backward_policy_rnDeriv, DEC-141), and this file is a supplement reported 'partial'. I read every statement in the file against main.tex:196, :217-219, :225-233 and :731-766, and against the strict definitions it uses (IsEGFPolicy, egfKernel, IsEGF and inflow in EGF/Defs.lean:135-243; InflowAC in EGF/SamplingCorollaries.lean:626; inflowDensity, backwardWeight, backwardKernel, backward_policy, coordJac and map_eq_withDensity_abs_det in EGF/BackwardPolicy.lean:193-536; lamAc, acMap, acPolicy and printed_inflow_not_ac at :827-886). (1) IsEGFPolicy.bind_eq_sum_map (:82) states mu pi = sum_i (Phi_i)_#(alpha^i mu) for any measure mu and measurable Phi_i. That is the mathematics of main.tex:747-752 with no inverse, and it matches target item (1) exactly. (2) inflow_ac_of_map_ac (:143) and InflowAC.of_map_ac (:235) have exactly the signatures of target item (2): IsEGFPolicy, (Phi_i)_# lam << lam for all i, and F_out << lam, with conclusion inflow << lam. There is no sigma-finiteness, no inverse and no Jacobian. Against C-6's corrected text ('F_in* = sum_i (Phi_i)_#(alpha^i F_out*) << lambda because each Phi_i is nonsingular'), the hypotheses are the added hypothesis of C-6 plus F_out << lambda, which is weaker than the paper's F_out = f_out lambda, plus the measurability of the moves and the weights, which IsEGFPolicy (strict, already audited) carries for every EGF. No hidden hypothesis. The clause 'hence f_in* exists' is a separate theorem, inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac (:223), under SigmaFinite lam (see finding 1). (3) inflow_ac_iff (:133) is an iff for each fixed F_out. It needs only IsEGFPolicy, and it is sharp. bind_ac_iff_map_ac (:176) needs alpha^i(s) > 0 everywhere. That suffices: lam << alpha^i lam, then AbsolutelyContinuous.map. It is the paper's softmax-head setting (l.288, :302). The theorem is correct as stated. The REPORT's gloss on it is not (finding 2). (4) inflow_ac_of_bind_ac, bind_withDensity_ac and inflow_ac_forall_iff are correct for any kernel. InflowAC.of_map_eq_withDensity (:243) really has the hypotheses of strict EGF.inflowAC_of_isEGFPolicy (SamplingCorollaries.lean:898) minus hJm and hf, so it supersedes that anchor as claimed. (5) Instances. map_ac_of_leftInverse (:291) is sound: Phi^{-1}(A) is a subset of g(A), and Mathlib's addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn_of_addHaar_eq_zero applies. map_ac_of_differentiable, map_ac_of_diffeomorph (n != 0), map_ac_diffeoEquiv, map_ac_of_measurePreserving and InflowAC.of_{isEGF, quasiMeasurePreserving, measurePreserving, diffeomorph, equiv_addHaar} are all as their docstrings say. InflowAC.of_isEGF indeed needs no BorelSpace. (6) backward_policy_measurePreserving (:370) is EGF.backward_policy at J = 1 with hJ discharged by MeasurePreserving.map_eq and withDensity_one. It has the four conclusions verbatim and no sigma-finiteness. The added hypothesis 'measure-preserving' is the reason for 'partial'. The REPORT notes disclose it, but the docstring checklist does not (finding 3). inflowDensity_one and backwardWeight_one unfold to the printed l.736-737 with |J| = 1. rnDeriv_map_ae_eq_one needs sigma-finite lam. coordJac_ae_eq_one is for Haar measure, a differentiable inverse and a measure-preserving Phi_i, and its proof is correct (withDensity_eq_iff_of_sigmaFinite). (7) Findings about the paper. That the printed formula of l.735-737 holds with |J| = 1 for measure-preserving moves is right in both readings of |J| (C-8, C-10). That every experiment uses such moves is right: l.432 and :440 (affine SL_2(Z) maps and translations of T^2), l.493 (the minimal four affine maps), l.496 (rotations of S^2). The ablation, which the REPORT does not cite, also uses such moves: main.tex:1210-1211, :1310-1311 and :1413-1414 take S = R^2 with 8 translations and Lebesgue measure. So the claim survives. Cite those lines too. The refutation EGF.printed_inflow_not_ac satisfies IsEGFPolicy (isEGFPolicy_acPolicy) and F_out = lamAc.withDensity 1 << lamAc. not_map_ac_acMap (:402) derives the failure of nonsingularity from printed_inflow_not_ac.2.2.2.2.1, the '¬ F_in << lamAc' conjunct, through inflow_ac_of_map_ac with the other two hypotheses discharged. So the counterexample violates exactly that hypothesis. (8) Non-vacuity. doubling_witness is a genuine witness, not a vacuous statement. IsEGFPolicy for p = 1 with weight 1 is built by isEGFPolicy_egfKernel. Measure preservation comes from AddCircle.ergodic_nsmul with n = 2. Non-injectivity is proved by 2*(T/2) = 0. So the hypotheses of inflow_ac_of_map_ac are satisfiable by a non-invertible move, and EGF.backward_policy (S ≃ᵐ S) cannot reach it. bind_ac_iff_map_ac's hpos is met by the uniform policy. backward_policy_measurePreserving's hypotheses are met by translations. None of the hypotheses is unsatisfiable, and no conclusion hides in a structure field.

corrections.notes: Both prove the << clause of C-6's corrected text, with fewer hypotheses than it lists: any measurable space, measurable Phi_i, F_out << lambda. There is no hidden hypothesis. The closing 'hence f_in* exists' is inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac (:223), which needs SigmaFinite lam, and the REPORT does not name it among C-6's anchors. See finding 1. C-6's status 'found' and its anchor switch from EGF.inflowAC_of_isEGFPolicy are the master's to record. InflowAC.of_map_eq_withDensity proves that the old anchor's hypotheses imply the new ones, so the switch loses nothing.

corrections.notes: Every supporting statement is correct. Nonsingularity plus measurability is Mathlib's QuasiMeasurePreserving (Measurable f ∧ μa.map f ≪ μb), as claimed. The REPORT's prose gloss 'cannot be weakened to a condition on lambda alone' overstates bind_ac_iff_map_ac (finding 2). For the master's register, not the closer's: C-7's corrected text ('or any lambda equivalent to Lebesgue measure') gives (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda but not, without sigma-finiteness, the density f_in that the theorem's formula needs. Its own anchor EGF.backward_policy_rnDeriv carries [SigmaFinite lam] (finding 1).

findings.where: REPORT.json corrections[C-6].notes and labels[0].findings[0] ('This proves the corrected text of C-6'); InflowNonsingular.lean:223
findings.what: inflow_ac_of_map_ac and InflowAC.of_map_ac prove the << clause of C-6 with no hidden hypothesis. C-6's corrected text, however, ends 'hence f_in* exists', and that clause is inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac, which needs [SigmaFinite lam]. It must: on R take lambda = Leb|(0,1) + ∞•Leb|(R∖(0,1)), Phi(x) = x + 1, alpha = 1, f_out = 1_(0,1). Then lambda is equivalent to Lebesgue, Phi is nonsingular, F_out = f_out lambda = Leb|(0,1) is finite, and F_in = Leb|(1,2) << lambda. Yet F_in((1,2)) = 1, while every lambda.withDensity g gives (1,2) mass 0 or ∞, so f_in does not exist. This is harmless under def:egf's Riemannian volume, which is sigma-finite. It does bear on C-7's corrected text 'or any lambda equivalent to Lebesgue measure', whose anchor EGF.backward_policy_rnDeriv carries [SigmaFinite lam].
findings.fix: In REPORT/curation, name EGF.inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac as the anchor of C-6's 'hence f_in* exists' clause, with its sigma-finite lambda. The master may add 'sigma-finite' to the 'lambda equivalent to Lebesgue' examples of C-6/C-7 in corrections.toml (a register edit, not the closer's).

findings.where: REPORT.json labels[0].findings[1] ('so C-6/C-7's added hypothesis cannot be weakened to a condition on lambda alone'); InflowNonsingular.lean:174-185
findings.what: bind_ac_iff_map_ac is correctly stated: positive weights give lam pi << lam iff every move is nonsingular. Through inflow_ac_forall_iff, nonsingularity is therefore necessary for 'every F_out << lambda has F_in << lambda'. The gloss is false as written, though. Conditions on lambda alone do imply nonsingularity of every move in the paper's class: lambda equivalent to Lebesgue does for diffeomorphisms (EGF.map_ac_of_equiv_addHaar, C-7's own corrected text), and counting measure does for all maps. The sentence would reach the author as a fact contradicting C-7.
findings.fix: Replace the clause with: 'so nonsingularity is necessary; a condition on lambda suffices only if it implies it, which the printed lambda << Lebesgue does not (EGF.not_map_ac_acMap)'.

findings.where: InflowNonsingular.lean:46-55 (## Hypothesis checklist); REPORT.json labels[0].hypotheses (|J_s Phi_i^{-1}| marked 'carried')
findings.what: The checklist omits two hypotheses that some declarations add relative to the paper. (a) Measure-preserving moves, in backward_policy_measurePreserving (:370), inflow_eq_withDensity_measurePreserving (:386), coordJac_ae_eq_one (:332) and rnDeriv_map_ae_eq_one (:347). The paper's diffeomorphisms have an arbitrary Jacobian. This is the very reason the row is 'partial'. The REPORT notes disclose it, but its hypotheses row calls the |J| factor 'carried' rather than strengthened. (b) Sigma-finite lambda, in inflow_eq_withDensity_sum_rnDeriv (:205), inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac (:223) and rnDeriv_map_ae_eq_one. The checklist row 'lambda sigma-finite: ⚠ weakened, not assumed' is true only of backward_policy_measurePreserving. Both are disclosed elsewhere and no mark is claimed, hence minor.
findings.fix: Add two checklist rows marked '⚠ strengthened': 'Φᵢ diffeomorphisms, arbitrary |J| | measure-preserving measurable bijections (|J| = 1) in backward_policy_measurePreserving, inflow_eq_withDensity_measurePreserving', and 'λ (no σ-finiteness printed) | σ-finite in inflow_eq_withDensity_sum_rnDeriv, inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac, rnDeriv_map_ae_eq_one (necessary for the density)'. In REPORT, mark the |J| row 'strengthened'.
